MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MARCH 14, 2018

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present: Chair Schmitz, Pope, Combs, Lum, Munday, Vanden Bos, Wisot

  Committee Members Absent: Scott

  Staff Members Present:  Greg Grammer, Assistant City Manager
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy, Willdan
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present: Deputy Tami Bouse, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Lomita Station
  Sergeant Ricky Osburn, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Lomita Station

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS moved, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT to,

  APPROVE MINUTES OF THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEEETING OF
  MAY 10, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  Paul Moilanen, Hitching Post, stated that late last year he was in communication with Community
  Services Director, Andy Clark regarding the demolition of the Community Center and the parking lot
  on the corner of Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN) and Palos Verdes Drive East (PVDE), which is
  being used as a short-cut to interchange traffic and asked if the item was on this or a future agenda.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that it is not, but will look into this request.

  Jennifer Whynaucht , Hitching Post, (also present Nancy Parson, Principal, Dapplegray Elementary
  School) stated that she has two children who attend Dapplegray Elementary School and has
  concerns and solutions for the safety of pedestrians at peak arrival and departure times at
  Dapplegray Elementary School. Ms. Whynaucht stated that there are congestion and speeding
  issues on PVDN between PVDE and Narbonne Avenue and Rolling Hills. When traffic is not
  congested, drivers are travelling at 40+ miles per hour (mph) and are not paying attention. She is
  also concerned with the increased number of accidents where vehicles veer onto the walking path
  and crash into fences. Ms. Whynaucht provided some suggestions to increase safety: 1) that there
  be increased sheriff’s presence during peak hours to urge drivers to slow down; 2) to add a solar
  generated flashing beacon light (programmed to work during peak hours) to the top of the “25 MPH”
  sign to make it more visible for drivers; and 3) posting the speed board to remind drivers of the 25
  MPH zone. She stated that Assistant City Manager Grammer and Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
  have been working with her and another resident on this, it has been instituted, and has already
  made a significant difference. In addition, Assistant City Manager Grammer has notified the Sheriff’s
  Department who have provided increased patrolling in the area. Ms. Whynaucht stated that they
  are also requesting a flashing light when the button is pressed at the crosswalk at the Dapplegray
  Elementary School entrance. Ms. Whynaucht added that Assistant Manager Grammer and Traffic
  Engineering Deputy Itagaki have also added a “25 MPH” sign between Strawberry Lane and
  Dapplegray School.

  Nancy Parsons, Principal, Dapplegray Elementary School, provided letters regarding concerns.

5.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST – TRAFFIC SIGNS AND GUARDRAIL REVIEW

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that due to several changes on Palos Verdes Drive East,
  he requested an inventory on the signs and guardrails to assess any necessary changes.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a PowerPoint presentation on this item and provided an
  overview of the existing signs which were inventoried to determine which signs could be removed
  and which signs need to be installed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS inquired about several “no parking” signs near the Rolling
  Hills Country Club since the site is changing. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that those
  are existing signs that were likely installed so that Country Club Members would not park there.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that there were no planned changes to the signs but this
  could be discussed.

Traffic & Safety Committee Meeting Minutes
March 14, 2018  1
   COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT stated that there is no signage indicating the entrance to the
  Country Club, and therefore, uses the “Slow Truck” sign as a marker to make a left into the club.
  There was a brief discussion on this item. Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that the number
  of signs could be reduced to one “No Parking” sign at both ends of the street and removal of any
  additional signs.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM stated that the bike lane on PVDE should be uniform since the lane
  is narrower in some places. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki clarified that that is not a bike lane
  and rather just an edge line. Deputy Bouse stated that the street would need to be widened to
  accommodate space for a bike lane. CHAIR SCHMIDT stated that installation for a bike lane could
  be a separate discussion.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that 5 criteria were looked at to install a guardrail, which
  included: collision history, roadway alignment, operating conditions, climate conditions, and
  roadside recovery area. The current function of the guardrail was reviewed. Looking at six years
  of collision history with only two incidents that would be considered to be “run off road”, it was
  determined that drivers are travelling safely and will likely remain the same without the guardrail
  since motorists are provided sufficient warning of the upcoming curve.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that her recommendations are to remove or fix the signs
  as noted on Exhibits 1 and 2 of the staff report and to retain the north side guardrail and repair a
  section of it and to remove the southbound guardrail on PVDE and remove the boulders that are
  between the guardrail and 3-rail fence.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS asked if the Traffic and Safety Committee is reviewing the
  removal or repair of the guardrail for aesthetic or cost purposes. Assistant City Manager Grammer
  stated that prior to making a decision on this, staff wanted the Committee to weigh in on this item
  and stated that if the guardrail remains it is necessary to make repairs.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT stated that if the guardrail is not needed then it should be removed
  and removing it will contribute to the rural look of the city.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked about the original installation of the guardrail and if
  perhaps, it was due to the utility pole that is there. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the
  pole was not likely the reason.

  Deputy Bouse stated that prior to the installation of the walking path, the guardrail made pedestrians
  feel more secure. Since the walking path is far from the road, the guardrail may not be necessary.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS commented that he is not opposed to removing the guardrail since
  there is enough of a buffer for vehicles that veer off. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki added that
  there is an elevation change from the street to the pedestrian trail.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM stated that he would like to discuss the possibility of a bike lane. The
  Traffic and Safety Committee agreed that this will be added to a future agenda for discussion.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  1. REMOVE, REPAIR OR REPLACE TRAFFIC SIGNS ON PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE EAST AS NOTED ON EXHIBITS A-1 AND A-2 OF THE STAFF
  REPORT;
  2. REMOVE THE GUARDRAIL ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE EAST AND REPAIR THE GUARDRAIL ON THE NORTH SIDE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  B. PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB / CHANDLER RANCH
  ROAD

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that the Country Club and its’ members are concerned with
  visibility issues upon exiting the Rolling Hills Country Club (RHCC). Last month there was an
  accident at the intersection. The (RHCC) has requested that 300 feet of the three-rail fencing be
  removed.

  Deputy Bouse stated that drivers are not paying attention when making the turn.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a PowerPoint presentation on this item and provided a
  report on her observations of the traffic and visibility at this site. Based on the design guidelines for
  40 MPH roads, motorists are provided with the required 300 feet of site distance.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that her recommendation is not to make any changes at
  the site at this time.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS inquired about the guidelines and anyone who may want to
  challenge that they were not provided sufficient site distance. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki

Traffic & Safety Committee Meeting Minutes
March 14, 2018  2
   stated that the design guidelines manual allows several choices and believes that there is sufficient
  support for 300 feet of site distance.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT stated that the problem is that there is no signage for the RHCC
  entrance. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that signage will be installed soon.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE confirmed that this was discussed by the Park and Activities
  Commission.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki suggested that a yellow diamond sign showing that an
  intersection is coming up may be a solution. However, it is difficult to decide since the RHCC signs
  have not been installed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT
  to,
  KEEP THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY
  CLUB/CHANDLER RANCH ROAD INTERSECTION AS IS UNTIL THE NEW SIGNAGE
  FOR THE ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB IS INSTALLED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  C. 702 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE – SHORT TIME LIMIT PARKING REQUEST

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that the business owners on Deep Valley Drive were polled
  about short term parking. Twenty-one were opposed and fifteen were in favor of the short-time limit
  parking sign.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT stated that the biggest impact is from the gym. This was brought
  up since most businesses in this area require less than 30-minute visits.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that it seems the sentiment of the business owners is to avoid any
  restrictions that may drive away customers.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE inquired about the initial request of the dry cleaners for (2) parking
  spaces.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked about having (1) parking space with a time limit. Traffic Engineering
  Deputy Itagaki stated that a green curb could be 9, 12, or 24 minute parking limit and stated that a
  limited parking space will cause visitors to shift where they are parking but also reminds longer-
  term visitors (for example, from the gym) to park in the parking lot.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ suggested speaking to the gym regarding the concerns that the businesses are
  having with members parking on the street since they may not be aware.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE suggested that (1) 30-minute parking space at either end may be
  helpful. A discussion on this comment was held.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY
  to,
  INSTALL (2) 30-MINUTE PARKING SPACES AT EITHER END OF DEEP VALLEY
  DRIVE AND TO HAVE A CONVERSATION WITH THE GYM OWNER REGARDING
  THE BUSINESS’ CONCERN WITH STREET PARKING ON DEEP VALLEY DRIVE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  D. HAWTHORNE BOULEVARD AND SILVER SPUR ROAD – PEDESTRIAN SIGNAL TIMING

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that there was a request for staff to look into having a
  pedestrian scramble at Silver Spur Road and Hawthorne Blvd.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she reviewed the accident history and there have
  been no pedestrian collisions at this intersection. Willdan staff looked at the guidelines to install a
  pedestrian scramble and conducted an observation of the site. A report on the observations was
  provided.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that this will cause a longer delay for traffic.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ commented that the pedestrian scramble may cause pedestrians to have a false
  sense of how much time they have to cross. In addition, in her observation drivers are respectful of
  the children crossing during school hours and has not seen anything dangerous.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that there is an issue with turning right going up from Silver
  Spur to Hawthorne Blvd. during peak hours and asked if there is a possibility of having a right-turn
  arrow installed. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there may be a possibility but there
  are concerns with doing this.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked about the length of time for the current signal. Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Itagaki stated that it may be a 90-second cycle with most of the green-time going to Hawthorne Blvd.

Traffic & Safety Committee Meeting Minutes
March 14, 2018  3
   COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN
  BOS to,

  APPROVE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION TO NOT INSTALL THE PEDESTRIAN
  SCRAMBLE AT HAWTHORNE BLVD. AND SILVER SPUR ROAD AT THIS TIME.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  E. DEEP VALLEY DRIVE AT POST OFFICE – NO PEDESTRIAN CROSSING SIGNS

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that this is item is related to concerns about “jaywalking”
  on Deep Valley Drive adjacent to the post office.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that pedestrians crossing at this location is not jaywalking.
  The code states that a pedestrian who crosses in the middle of a block that has controlled
  intersections at each end is considered to be jaywalking. Sergeant Osburn and Deputy Bouse
  confirmed this.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that in her observation, most post office customers park in
  the parking lot.

  Sergeant Osburn stated that the mailbox outside of the post office has a high incidence of theft.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM asked if a crosswalk could be considered. Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Itagaki stated that she discourages installing crosswalks without a controlled signal.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  WISOT to,

  LEAVE THE SIGNS AS THEY ARE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

6.  DISCUSSION ITEMS (VERBAL REPORTS)

  A. SCHOOL SIGNS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that he met with Ms. Whynaucht and the City has
  installed an additional 25 MPH when children are present parking sign on PVDN.

  Ms. Parsons stated that anything the Traffic and Safety could do would be appreciated and asked
  about getting her item on the agenda. Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that he and Traffic
  Engineering Deputy Itagaki will review her request.

  Ms. Whynaucht stated that enforcing traffic can be controlled and installing flashing beacons would
  be helpful during peak hours.

  Ms. Parsons inquired about having a traffic control officer at the entrance to the school or having the
  left turn light extended. Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that the light can be extended and
  will look into this.

  Sergeant Osburn stated that a portion of PVDN will be closed in July for the CalWater Pipeline
  Project and that the City of Lomita will be undertaking a street improvement project on PCH over
  the summer.

  B. RECTANGULAR RAPID FLASH BEACON – INTERIM APPROVAL TERMINATION

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that Caltrans had an interim approval through the Federal
  Highway Administration to allow rectangular rapid flash beacons and that approval has been
  terminated. Cities may keep the ones that are existing until the end of their useful life.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE asked about other options. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
  stated that the round flashing beacons and LED signs are other options.

  C. COYOTES

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT stated that he is concerned about coyotes and small pets and
  children. CHAIR SCHMIDT stated that the city has a contract in place with LA County and provided
  an update on the escalation process in place for dealing with coyotes. COMMITTEE MEMBER
  WISOT commented that many residents do not know how to properly haze coyotes.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that there will be a Peninsula wide Coyote Workshop on
  April 18, 2018. The goal is to have volunteers assist with hazing. CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that there
  is an effort to get the word out which includes reaching the HOAs. CHAIR SCHMITZ added that the
  City’s website has information and videos about coyotes.

Traffic & Safety Committee Meeting Minutes
March 14, 2018  4
   COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE stated that it is frustrating to see posts on Nextdoor that the City is
  not doing anything and thanked staff for their efforts.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that there is a vacancy on the Traffic and Safety
  Committee. Inquiries can be directed to Heidi Luce, City Clerk.

7.  COMMITTEE REPORTS (VERBAL REPORTS)

  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE stated that the intersection at Silver Spur and Monte Malaga a
  pedestrian signal installed and stated that it has been helpful but there may be some visibility issues
  at that location due to overgrown vegetation.

8.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  NONE

9.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:55 p.m.

  ___________________________
  Carol Corea
  Administrative Assistant
